images.caption: Figure 1:MotorMind: Equipping general-purpose vision-language models into robot controller.VLM proposes mid-level actions (e.g. "move forward by 12.20mm"), then pass to the control layer that connects those decisions to physical execution and feedback. Asynchronous monitoring enables interruption of pending actions, and outcome verification guides recovery and replanning. This design supports zero-shot manipulation across simulation and real-world settings without task-specific training.
Figure 2:Diagnosing VLM capabilities for robotic manipulation.We evaluate action selection, progress assessment, and subgoal completion.

header: 3MotorMind: VLM Harness for Zero-Shot Robotic Manipulation

images.caption: Figure 3:Overview ofMotorMind.The Planner specifies subgoals and success criteria. The Executor proposes short action batches, which the Controller converts into robot motion. During execution, the Monitor evaluates updated observations and can request interruption at an action boundary, cancelling pending commands. Outcome assessment then determines whether to advance, retry, or replan. Memory summarizes execution evidence and assessed outcomes in the background for subsequent decisions.
